items.title: Musk, Uber co-founder join call for Jensen Huang's return to Nvidia
items.summary: Tech tycoon Elon Musk and an Uber co-founder are, as of Sunday, among more than 158,000 signatories of an open letter calling for Jensen Huang's reinstatement as Nvidia chief.In Washington, however, US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent argued Sunday that Nvidia should look "outside" the company for its next chief.

items.summary: Alphabet could buy Uber Technologies, combining its Waymo robotaxi business with America’s largest ride-hailing network, Reuters Breakingviews columnist Jennifer Saba argued Tuesday. items.title: Alibaba vs. Uber Technologies: Which Tech Platform Stock Is a Better Buy for 2027?
items.summary: Alibaba and Uber both lead their markets, but one trades at a far lower earnings multiple while the other is priced for sustained high growth.

items.title: Nvidia lost $1.6 trillion after Jensen Huang's exit, but Apple's and Uber's CEO transitions offer a blueprint
items.summary: Nvidia interim CEO Colette Kress has big shoes to fill following Jensen Huang’s resignation. But the leadership transitions at Apple and Uber offer reasons for optimism.

items.title: MercadoLibre vs. Uber Technologies: Which Consumer Network Stock Is a Better Buy for 2027?
items.summary: MercadoLibre's 47% revenue surge stands out, but Uber's cheaper earnings multiple and steadier balance sheet make the 2027 call far closer than the growth numbers suggest.

items.title: Alphabet (GOOGL) Faces Uber Deal Talk, Space Chip Test And €1.66 Billion Fine
items.summary: Alphabet (NasdaqGS:GOOGL) is reportedly exploring a potential tie-up with Uber that could combine the rideshare network with Waymo's autonomous technology. Google has unveiled "Project Suncatcher", an orbital experiment designed to test its AI accelerator chips in space-based data centers. The group faces renewed legal attention around a €1.66b EU advertising fine while Tesla's robotaxis now operate ahead of Waymo in Texas. items.title: Uber Says Personal Data Was Exposed in Third-Party Data Breach
items.summary: The transportation company said an unauthorized third party had compromised a service provider’s internal credentials and used them to access Uber’s account, according to a notice on the California attorney general’s website dated Tuesday.
